title: Consequence-Based Review Gate
summary: Scale evidence, independence, expertise, approval, monitoring, and rollback to the realistic harm caused by an incorrect AI-assisted result.
prerequisites: A proposed AI-assisted output or action and its intended use

sections.title: Classify consequence before reviewing
paragraphs: Estimate credible harm across people, safety, rights, privacy, money, operations, security, compliance, reputation, and reversibility. Include scale, affected groups, detectability, time to recovery, and whether an error can trigger an external action. Do not lower the level because the output sounds confident or the model is usually accurate.

Low consequence work may need a reasonableness check. Moderate consequence work needs source comparison, tests, edge cases, and a named reviewer. High consequence work needs current authoritative evidence, independent review, relevant domain expertise, explicit approval, a safe execution boundary, monitoring, and a tested rollback or recovery plan.

These labels are a practical review-planning scale, not universal legal thresholds and not professional legal, safety, security, or compliance advice. Use the highest credible consequence when uncertainty remains. A model's confidence, a reviewer's familiarity with the tool, and a low historical error rate do not establish a low consequence. The NIST Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework provides broader risk-management context at https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework.

Worked case: A fictional company operates a local, offline documentation workstation. An AI assistant proposes archive-manifest-v2 version 2, which would copy exactly synthetic-ops/incoming/alpha.txt, synthetic-ops/incoming/beta.txt, and synthetic-ops/incoming/gamma.txt to synthetic-ops/archive/. This is an exact three-file allowlist, not a wildcard authorization. The proposed boundary permits no other file, source, destination, version, deletion, publication, network transfer, source modification, or privileged action. Mina and Omar are the two fictional operations users who rely on the archive for internal troubleshooting. Elena Ruiz is the accountable Operations Owner, Sam Lee is the Automation Author, and Priya Nair is the Independent Operations Reviewer. No real users, personal data, external service, or production system is part of the exercise.

For the initial case, a mistaken selection could produce incorrect archive contents, omit troubleshooting information, or waste Mina's and Omar's time. The source files are intended to remain unchanged, and an erroneous local archive copy can ordinarily be removed. The consequence classification is LOW only because the described action is local, non-privileged, non-external, limited to three synthetic files, readily detectable, and recoverable within the stated boundary. This classifies the proposed use, not the AI assistant, provider, or model family.

The classification changes when the inputs or intended use change. Copying 50,000 operational records locally may be MODERATE because scale, affected groups, detectability, and recovery time increase even if the operation remains reversible. Deleting originals, publishing a customer-facing status note, changing access, or sending files to an external destination is HIGH for this exercise because an error can cause an external effect, irreversible loss, or disclosure. Removing a local copy cannot make an external recipient forget or destroy information already received. Prevention and containment must therefore precede an irreversible action through a deny-by-default boundary, an exact human-approved target list, a dry run, least privilege, a human-controlled hold, and a stop mechanism.

The offline exercise in the section titled Expected evidence and verification uses Python 3 standard-library fixtures named PROPOSAL, GOOD_APPROVAL, BAD_APPROVAL, GOOD_REVIEW, and BAD_REVIEW. It checks an independently fixed policy for the copy operation, relative source and destination paths, the exact three-file scope, disabled network access, no source deletion, and no external publication. The program itself performs no copy, deletion, recovery, or network operation. Its booleans are fictional supplied attestations, not proof that testing, review, approval, or recovery occurred. Python's standard-library documentation for the mechanisms used is available at https://docs.python.org/3/library/copy.html, https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html, and https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#isinstance.

The exercise includes meaningful negative cases for proposal identifier, version, expiry, exact scope, operation, source, destination, external-publication status, reviewer independence, approver identity and role, missing or malformed records, invalid booleans, invalid dates and scopes, absent evidence, unsafe boundary flags, unrecorded attestations, and jointly changed records that agree with one another but violate the independent policy. No execution is claimed here. If the supplied program is run with Python 3 and all assertions pass, its exact expected output is:
failed gate: approval version mismatch; approval is stale; reviewer is not independent; evidence version mismatch
repaired gate: APPROVE
bounded scope: archive-manifest-v2, 3 synthetic files, local reversible copy

Changed-input learner task: Start from archive-manifest-v2 version 2, but change the exact manifest to four files: synthetic-ops/incoming/alpha.txt, synthetic-ops/incoming/beta.txt, synthetic-ops/incoming/gamma.txt, and synthetic-ops/incoming/delta.txt. Change the destination to external-status.example/upload/ and add an action that publishes a generated status note after upload. The only supplied approval remains Elena Ruiz's fictional fixture approval through 2026-09-20 for the original three-file copy from synthetic-ops/incoming/ to synthetic-ops/archive/, with no external publication. Priya Nair's supplied review fixture also covers only that original local scope. Complete every field of a new gate record and select APPROVE, REVISE, REJECT, or ESCALATE. Explain the consequence, affected people and systems, credible harms, reversibility, evidence and expertise required, approval status, prevention or containment boundary, monitoring and stop signal, and response if disclosure occurs.

Changed-input answer key: Decision: REJECT the changed action as submitted, or ESCALATE it for a newly designed high-consequence review. Do not APPROVE. Consequence level: HIGH for this exercise because the action expands from three files to four, changes a local destination to an external destination, and triggers publication. Affected scope: the four source files, the workstation, the external service or recipient, and people who may rely on the generated status note. Credible harms include disclosure, publication of incorrect information, operational confusion, security exposure, compliance impact, and reputational harm. Whether the files contain protected or confidential information and which organizational, legal, or regulatory requirements apply are UNKNOWN until established. The supplied approval is not expired on the exercise date of 2026-09-19, but it is still invalid for the changed action because its file list, destination, external-publication status, evidence scope, and execution boundary do not match. Priya's old review is mismatched for the same reasons.

Changed-input answer key, required controls: Obtain current authoritative data-handling requirements for the actual organization and destination, an exact-manifest comparison, content and recipient tests, edge-case tests, independent review appropriate to the higher consequence, relevant domain expertise, security review of the external boundary, and explicit owner approval bound to the exact four files, operation, source, destination, publication behavior, version, and expiry. Prevent upload by default. Require a dry run, an exact allowlist, least privilege, no automatic publication, and a human-controlled hold. Stop on any unexpected file, content classification, recipient, destination, network state, version, evidence, reviewer, or approval mismatch. If disclosure occurs, contain further access and notify the accountable response role under the applicable procedure. Deleting an uploaded object is containment, not proof that disclosure was reversed. This decision is traceable to the expanded scope, external destination, publication trigger, mismatched approval and review, and unresolved data classification, not to model confidence or a boolean severity score.
sections.callout: This provider-neutral case classifies the consequence of one exact proposed use. Changing the provider does not transfer evidence or approval and does not alter the fixed three-file boundary.

sections.title: Complete the review gate
paragraphs: Use safe labels for protected data and link to authorized evidence. A model-provided risk rating is input to the gate, not the final authorization decision.

Complete the record before any real action. In this worked case, every person, approval, review, test flag, and recovery flag is a fictional fixture value. The hypothetical record concerns only archive-manifest-v2 version 2 and an expiry at the end of 2026-09-20. Its exact proposed scope is copying synthetic-ops/incoming/alpha.txt, synthetic-ops/incoming/beta.txt, and synthetic-ops/incoming/gamma.txt from synthetic-ops/incoming/ to synthetic-ops/archive/. It authorizes no wildcard, additional file, changed path, later version, deletion, source modification, publication, network transfer, external destination, or privileged operation.

Worked gate record: Output or action: Execute archive-manifest-v2 version 2 to copy exactly synthetic-ops/incoming/alpha.txt, synthetic-ops/incoming/beta.txt, and synthetic-ops/incoming/gamma.txt to synthetic-ops/archive/. Affected people and systems: Mina and Omar, one fictional offline documentation workstation, and the three synthetic files. Credible harms: incorrect archive contents, missing troubleshooting information, wasted operator time, or unintended source modification. No safety, rights, privacy, money, external security, or public-disclosure impact is expected if the stated synthetic and offline boundary is authentic, but the supplied fixtures do not prove that broader impacts are impossible. Reversibility and recovery time: the proposed procedure is to verify that the sources are unchanged, remove only the three recorded archive copies, verify their removal, and stop and escalate if any other file would be affected. Recovery time on the target workstation is UNKNOWN until observed there. Consequence level: LOW for the exact local, non-privileged, detectable, three-file action described. Required evidence: the authentic version-2 manifest, source-to-destination comparison, dry-run result, filename edge-case results, hash or byte comparison for the three exact fixtures, target-boundary observations, and an actual recovery transcript tied to the same fixture, version, scope, command, observer, and workstation. Required reviewer: PEER, specifically Priya Nair, independently of Sam Lee's authorship, subject to authentic identity and independence validation. Approval before action: Elena Ruiz, Operations Owner, for archive-manifest-v2 version 2 only, through 2026-09-20, subject to authentic authority, identity, scope, and freshness validation. Execution boundary: READ-ONLY for the three source files and REVERSIBLE for the three local archive copies, with no privilege, network, deletion, publication, or external destination. Monitoring and stop signal: stop before the first copy if any operation, source, destination, file count, file name, content comparison, version, reviewer, approval, expiry, or network state differs from the record; stop after a copy if an unexpected destination file appears or any source changes. Rollback or recovery: apply the proposed exact-file removal procedure only after independently validating it against the real target boundary; the fixture's recovery_tested value is a fictional supplied attestation, not evidence that recovery was performed. Decision: APPROVE only as the hypothetical expected fixture result, bounded to version 2, the three exact files, the two relative local paths, and the stated expiry. It is not authorization for a real action.

Before any real action, independently establish that the proposal, evidence, reviewer, approver, execution boundary, and recovery evidence are authentic and applicable to the target workstation. Until that validation occurs, actual approval and actual recovery evidence are UNKNOWN, and the simulation's printed APPROVE result must not be used as authorization. If authentic evidence is absent, mismatched, or not reproducible, the operational decision is REVISE, REJECT, or ESCALATE rather than APPROVE.

The record preserves uncertainty rather than converting an attestation into evidence. The supplied tests_passed and recovery_tested booleans report what a fictional fixture claims. They do not show a command, output, observation, reviewer action, recovery attempt, elapsed recovery time, or real approval. The exercise performs no copy, deletion, recovery, or network operation. A real evidence package must identify the exact fixture, proposal identifier, version, file list, paths, command or observation, result, reviewer, approver, date, expiry, execution boundary, and target environment.

Approval does not transfer when data, audience, automation, operation, source, destination, file list, version, publication behavior, network state, or external effect changes. A reviewer cannot independently review their own work when independence is required. The changed four-file external-publication task therefore needs a new record, new evidence, appropriately independent and expert review, and a new exact-scope approval. The original fictional approval cannot authorize delta.txt or external-status.example/upload/ even though it has not reached its stated expiry.

sections.callout: The completed record is a hypothetical fixture decision. It becomes relevant to a real action only after authentic evidence, reviewer independence, approval authority, exact scope, target behavior, and recovery evidence have been independently validated.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Challenge the classification with a plausible worst case and an affected-user perspective. Verify every required check actually ran, reviewers are independent enough for the consequence, approval is fresh, and rollback works in the real boundary. Reclassify when scope, data, audience, automation, or external impact changes.

The expected evidence is a review record linking the consequence level to required evidence, qualified reviewers, approval, execution controls, monitoring, and recovery. The final decision names an accountable person or role.

Challenge the classification with a plausible worst case and an affected-user perspective. Verify every required check actually ran, reviewers are independent enough for the consequence, approval is fresh, and recovery works in the real boundary. Reclassify when scope, data, audience, automation, or external impact changes.

Failed-gate example: The first submitted record was for archive-manifest-v2, but Elena's approval named version 1 and expired on 2026-09-18. The submitted manifest remained limited to alpha.txt, beta.txt, and gamma.txt, but the approval and evidence were not aligned to version 2. Sam Lee was listed as both author and reviewer. The dry-run evidence referred to fixture set v1 rather than the submitted manifest. The gate therefore fails on approval version, approval freshness, evidence match, and independence. The correct decision is REVISE or REJECT, not APPROVE. Model confidence cannot fill any of these evidence gaps.

Repaired evidence: Sam produced a new version-2 manifest containing only alpha.txt, beta.txt, and gamma.txt. Priya independently compared that manifest with the visible fixture, confirmed the exact operation, source and destination paths, external-publication flag, and file list, reviewed the dry-run and edge-case results, and confirmed that the recovery procedure targets only the three archive copies. Elena issued a fresh approval for version 2 with the exact scope and expiry of 2026-09-20. The bounded decision is APPROVE for this local reversible action only. The approval does not cover delta.txt, a changed source or destination, deletion, publication, network transfer, a later version, or any scope expansion.

Matching untrusted records are not sufficient. The exercise binds the proposal to independent scenario policy constants for the permitted copy operation, local source, local destination, three-file scope, disabled network, no source deletion, and no external publication. If the proposal, approval, and review are all changed to the same external destination or other operation, their agreement does not override that fixed boundary.

The following offline exercise checks these supplied fixture records mechanically. Its printed approval is an expected simulation result, not evidence that the checks, attestations, approval, review, recovery procedure, or target-workstation observations actually occurred. The simulation performs no file operation and makes no network call. It distinguishes a local simulated preflight from authorization to act on a real target workstation.

Run the exercise with Python 3 using only the standard library. Save the code as gate_simulation.py and run python3 gate_simulation.py. If all assertions pass, the exact expected output is:
failed gate: approval version mismatch; approval is stale; reviewer is not independent; evidence version mismatch
repaired gate: APPROVE
bounded scope: archive-manifest-v2, 3 synthetic files, local reversible copy

The assertions include an independent passing fixture and meaningful negative fixtures. They cover proposal-identifier mismatch, version and expiry failures, mismatched approval and evidence fields, unauthorized or non-independent identities, missing and malformed records, strict boolean validation, invalid dates and scopes, absent evidence, unsafe boundary flags, unrecorded test attestations, and jointly changed records. Null evidence_scope produces a controlled evidence scope diagnostic rather than a TypeError. Numeric 0 is rejected where a strict boolean is required rather than being accepted as equal to False.

Changed-input learner task: Keep the proposal identifier and version, then change the proposed action so that the manifest includes delta.txt, making four files; the destination becomes external-status.example/upload/; and the action publishes a generated status note after upload. The only available approval still names the original three-file local scope and expires 2026-09-20. Priya's review still covers the original three-file local fixture. Complete a new gate record and choose APPROVE, REVISE, REJECT, or ESCALATE. Explain the changed consequence, affected users and systems, prevention or containment boundary, evidence and expertise now required, missing approval, stop signal, and why removing a local copy would not recover an external disclosure.

Graduated hints: Hint 1: Compare the new destination, audience, and action trigger with the original READ-ONLY and REVERSIBLE boundary. Hint 2: Compare every approved file and path with the four-file external scope. A valid approval for the old scope cannot authorize the new scope. Hint 3: Ask which harms remain after a mistaken upload. Prevention and containment must happen before upload; later deletion cannot guarantee that a recipient did not retain a copy. Hint 4: A new record needs current authoritative data-handling requirements for the actual organization and destination, exact-manifest comparison, content and recipient tests, edge cases, independent review appropriate to the higher consequence, relevant domain expertise, security review for the external boundary, explicit owner approval for this exact version and expiry, monitoring, and a tested containment procedure.

Reasoned answer key: Decision: REJECT the proposed action as submitted, or ESCALATE for a newly designed high-consequence review. Do not APPROVE. Consequence: HIGH for this exercise because the changed action adds an external destination, expands the file scope, and triggers publication. A wrong selection could disclose content and affect recipients outside the workstation. The original low-consequence classification no longer applies. Affected people and systems: the four source files, the workstation, the external recipient or service, and any people who rely on the generated status note. Whether the files contain protected or confidential information is UNKNOWN and must be established before any upload. The existing approval is mismatched to both scope and destination, and Priya's evidence covers only the old fixture. Required work includes current authoritative data-handling requirements for the actual organization and destination, exact-manifest comparison, content and recipient tests, edge cases, independent review, relevant domain expertise, security review for the external boundary, explicit owner approval for this exact version and expiry, monitoring, and a tested containment procedure. The exercise does not establish which legal or regulatory requirements apply. Prevent upload by default. Use a dry run, an exact allowlist, least privilege, no automatic publication, and a human-controlled hold. Stop on any unexpected file, recipient, destination, content classification, network state, version, or approval mismatch. If disclosure occurs, contain access and notify the accountable response role under the applicable procedure. Do not claim that deletion or rollback undoes disclosure. The answer is based on changed consequences and traceable evidence gaps, not on a boolean severity score or model confidence.

Pass criteria: The learner identifies the scope expansion, external destination, publication trigger, and loss of local reversibility; classifies the changed case as HIGH or escalates it for high-consequence review; rejects the mismatched approval; marks data classification and applicable requirements UNKNOWN where not established; requires prevention and containment before upload; names independent review, relevant expertise, explicit approval, monitoring, and tested recovery or incident containment; and does not claim that rollback reverses disclosure. Error feedback: APPROVE means the learner treated an old approval as transferable. LOW or MODERATE without addressing external publication means the learner missed the changed consequence. Calling deletion a recovery means the learner confused local cleanup with reversal of disclosure. Treating model confidence or a boolean flag as evidence means the learner skipped human verification.

Implementation references: Python documents independent deep copying at https://docs.python.org/3/library/copy.html, date objects at https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html, runtime type checks at https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#isinstance, set subset checks at https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#frozenset.issubset, and string trimming at https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str.strip. These standard-library references explain the mechanisms used by the offline exercise. They do not validate the fictional fixture attestations or authorize a real operation.
Verification rigor follows consequence, not convenience.

code.label: Offline fixture, fixed-policy gate, and assertion-backed negative tests
code.code:
from copy import deepcopy
from datetime import date

# Fixed simulation date and independent scenario policy.
RUN_DATE = date(2026, 9, 19)
POLICY_OPERATION = "copy"
POLICY_SOURCE = "synthetic-ops/incoming/"
POLICY_DESTINATION = "synthetic-ops/archive/"
POLICY_SCOPE = (
    "synthetic-ops/incoming/alpha.txt",
    "synthetic-ops/incoming/beta.txt",
    "synthetic-ops/incoming/gamma.txt",
)
AUTHORIZED_APPROVER = "Elena Ruiz"
AUTHORIZED_ROLE = "Operations Owner"

PROPOSAL_KEYS = {
    "id", "version", "author", "operation", "scope", "source",
    "destination", "external_publication", "network", "deletes_source",
    "tests_passed", "recovery_tested",
}
APPROVAL_KEYS = {
    "proposal_id", "version", "approver", "role", "expires", "operation",
    "source", "destination", "external_publication", "scope",
}
REVIEW_KEYS = {
    "reviewer", "evidence_version", "evidence_scope", "evidence_operation",
    "evidence_source", "evidence_destination",
    "evidence_external_publication",
}

# These are simulated fixture attestations, not actual authorization or proof
# that a test, review, recovery procedure, or target operation occurred.
PROPOSAL = {
    "id": "archive-manifest-v2",
    "version": 2,
    "author": "Sam Lee",
    "operation": POLICY_OPERATION,
    "scope": POLICY_SCOPE,
    "source": POLICY_SOURCE,
    "destination": POLICY_DESTINATION,
    "external_publication": False,
    "network": False,
    "deletes_source": False,
    "tests_passed": True,
    "recovery_tested": True,
}

BAD_APPROVAL = {
    "proposal_id": "archive-manifest-v2",
    "version": 1,
    "approver": AUTHORIZED_APPROVER,
    "role": AUTHORIZED_ROLE,
    "expires": date(2026, 9, 18),
    "operation": POLICY_OPERATION,
    "source": POLICY_SOURCE,
    "destination": POLICY_DESTINATION,
    "external_publication": False,
    "scope": POLICY_SCOPE,
}

GOOD_APPROVAL = {
    "proposal_id": "archive-manifest-v2",
    "version": 2,
    "approver": AUTHORIZED_APPROVER,
    "role": AUTHORIZED_ROLE,
    "expires": date(2026, 9, 20),
    "operation": POLICY_OPERATION,
    "source": POLICY_SOURCE,
    "destination": POLICY_DESTINATION,
    "external_publication": False,
    "scope": POLICY_SCOPE,
}

BAD_REVIEW = {
    "reviewer": "Sam Lee",
    "evidence_version": 1,
    "evidence_scope": POLICY_SCOPE,
    "evidence_operation": POLICY_OPERATION,
    "evidence_source": POLICY_SOURCE,
    "evidence_destination": POLICY_DESTINATION,
    "evidence_external_publication": False,
}

GOOD_REVIEW = {
    "reviewer": "Priya Nair",
    "evidence_version": 2,
    "evidence_scope": POLICY_SCOPE,
    "evidence_operation": POLICY_OPERATION,
    "evidence_source": POLICY_SOURCE,
    "evidence_destination": POLICY_DESTINATION,
    "evidence_external_publication": False,
}


def is_text(value):
    return isinstance(value, str) and bool(value.strip())


def is_positive_int(value):
    return type(value) is int and value >= 1


def exact_bool(value):
    return type(value) is bool


def is_scope(value):
    return (
        isinstance(value, (tuple, list))
        and bool(value)
        and all(is_text(item) for item in value)
    )


def same_identity(left, right):
    return left.strip().casefold() == right.strip().casefold()


def key_errors(record, required, label):
    errors = []
    missing = required.difference(record)
    unexpected = set(record).difference(required)
    if missing:
        errors.append(label + " incomplete")
    if unexpected:
        errors.append(label + " has unexpected fields")
    return errors


def shape_errors(proposal, approval, review):
    errors = []

    if not isinstance(proposal, dict):
        return ["proposal malformed"]
    errors.extend(key_errors(proposal, PROPOSAL_KEYS, "proposal"))
    for key in ("id", "author", "operation", "source", "destination"):
        if key in proposal and not is_text(proposal[key]):
            errors.append("proposal identity or path invalid")
    if "version" in proposal and not is_positive_int(proposal["version"]):
        errors.append("proposal version invalid")
    if "scope" in proposal and not is_scope(proposal["scope"]):
        errors.append("proposal scope invalid")
    for key in (
        "external_publication", "network", "deletes_source",
        "tests_passed", "recovery_tested",
    ):
        if key in proposal and not exact_bool(proposal[key]):
            errors.append("proposal boolean invalid")

    if not isinstance(approval, dict):
        return errors + ["approval missing or malformed"]
    errors.extend(key_errors(approval, APPROVAL_KEYS, "approval"))
    for key in (
        "proposal_id", "approver", "role", "operation", "source",
        "destination",
    ):
        if key in approval and not is_text(approval[key]):
            errors.append("approval identity or path invalid")
    if "version" in approval and not is_positive_int(approval["version"]):
        errors.append("approval version invalid")
    if "expires" in approval and type(approval["expires"]) is not date:
        errors.append("approval date invalid")
    if (
        "external_publication" in approval
        and not exact_bool(approval["external_publication"])
    ):
        errors.append("approval boolean invalid")
    if "scope" in approval and not is_scope(approval["scope"]):
        errors.append("approval scope invalid")

    if not isinstance(review, dict):
        return errors + ["review missing or malformed"]
    errors.extend(key_errors(review, REVIEW_KEYS, "review"))
    if "reviewer" in review and not is_text(review["reviewer"]):
        errors.append("reviewer identity invalid")
    if (
        "evidence_version" in review
        and not is_positive_int(review["evidence_version"])
    ):
        errors.append("evidence version invalid")
    if (
        "evidence_scope" in review
        and not is_scope(review["evidence_scope"])
    ):
        errors.append("evidence scope invalid")
    for key in (
        "evidence_operation", "evidence_source", "evidence_destination",
    ):
        if key in review and not is_text(review[key]):
            errors.append("evidence operation or path invalid")
    if (
        "evidence_external_publication" in review
        and not exact_bool(review["evidence_external_publication"])
    ):
        errors.append("evidence boolean invalid")

    return errors


def check(proposal, approval, review):
    failures = shape_errors(proposal, approval, review)
    if failures:
        return failures

    if approval["proposal_id"] != proposal["id"]:
        failures.append("approval proposal mismatch")
    if approval["version"] != proposal["version"]:
        failures.append("approval version mismatch")
    if approval["expires"] < RUN_DATE:
        failures.append("approval is stale")

    approval_matches = (
        approval["operation"] == proposal["operation"]
        and approval["source"] == proposal["source"]
        and approval["destination"] == proposal["destination"]
        and approval["external_publication"]
        == proposal["external_publication"]
        and tuple(approval["scope"]) == tuple(proposal["scope"])
    )
    if not approval_matches:
        failures.append("approval scope mismatch")

    if same_identity(review["reviewer"], proposal["author"]):
        failures.append("reviewer is not independent")

    if review["evidence_version"] != proposal["version"]:
        failures.append("evidence version mismatch")
    evidence_scope_matches = (
        tuple(review["evidence_scope"]) == tuple(proposal["scope"])
        and review["evidence_operation"] == proposal["operation"]
        and review["evidence_source"] == proposal["source"]
        and review["evidence_destination"] == proposal["destination"]
        and review["evidence_external_publication"]
        == proposal["external_publication"]
    )
    if not evidence_scope_matches:
        failures.append("evidence scope mismatch")

    # Independent policy checks prevent matching records from redefining the
    # fixed safe boundary.
    if proposal["operation"] != POLICY_OPERATION:
        failures.append("operation outside policy")
    if proposal["source"] != POLICY_SOURCE:
        failures.append("source outside policy")
    if proposal["destination"] != POLICY_DESTINATION:
        failures.append("destination outside policy")
    if tuple(proposal["scope"]) != POLICY_SCOPE:
        failures.append("scope expansion")
    if (
        proposal["network"]
        or proposal["deletes_source"]
        or proposal["external_publication"]
    ):
        failures.append("unsafe boundary")
    if proposal["tests_passed"] is not True:
        failures.append("tests not recorded as passed")
    if proposal["recovery_tested"] is not True:
        failures.append("recovery not recorded as tested")
    if (
        not same_identity(approval["approver"], AUTHORIZED_APPROVER)
        or approval["role"] != AUTHORIZED_ROLE
    ):
        failures.append("approver is not authorized")

    return failures


_ASSERT_FAILURE_OMITTED = object()


def assert_failure(
    name,
    expected,
    proposal=_ASSERT_FAILURE_OMITTED,
    approval=_ASSERT_FAILURE_OMITTED,
    review=_ASSERT_FAILURE_OMITTED,
):
    if proposal is _ASSERT_FAILURE_OMITTED:
        proposal = deepcopy(PROPOSAL)
    if approval is _ASSERT_FAILURE_OMITTED:
        approval = deepcopy(GOOD_APPROVAL)
    if review is _ASSERT_FAILURE_OMITTED:
        review = deepcopy(GOOD_REVIEW)
    actual = check(proposal, approval, review)
    assert expected in actual, name + ": " + repr(actual)


def changed(record, field, value):
    result = deepcopy(record)
    result[field] = value
    return result


def jointly_changed(field, evidence_field, value):
    proposal = changed(PROPOSAL, field, value)
    approval = changed(GOOD_APPROVAL, field, value)
    review = changed(GOOD_REVIEW, evidence_field, value)
    return proposal, approval, review


def negative_tests():
    approval_cases = (
        (
            "proposal identifier",
            "approval proposal mismatch",
            changed(GOOD_APPROVAL, "proposal_id", "archive-manifest-v1"),
        ),
        (
            "approval version",
            "approval version mismatch",
            changed(GOOD_APPROVAL, "version", 1),
        ),
        (
            "approval source",
            "approval scope mismatch",
            changed(GOOD_APPROVAL, "source", "other/"),
        ),
        (
            "approval destination",
            "approval scope mismatch",
            changed(GOOD_APPROVAL, "destination", "other/"),
        ),
        (
            "approval publication",
            "approval scope mismatch",
            changed(GOOD_APPROVAL, "external_publication", True),
        ),
        (
            "approval scope",
            "approval scope mismatch",
            changed(GOOD_APPROVAL, "scope", ("other.txt",)),
        ),
        (
            "approval operation",
            "approval scope mismatch",
            changed(GOOD_APPROVAL, "operation", "move"),
        ),
        (
            "approval expiry",
            "approval is stale",
            changed(GOOD_APPROVAL, "expires", date(2026, 9, 18)),
        ),
    )
    for name, expected, approval in approval_cases:
        assert_failure(name, expected, approval=approval)

    unauthorized = changed(GOOD_APPROVAL, "approver", "Visitor")
    unauthorized["role"] = "Visitor"
    assert_failure(
        "authorized approver", "approver is not authorized",
        approval=unauthorized,
    )

    review_cases = (
        (
            "independence",
            "reviewer is not independent",
            changed(GOOD_REVIEW, "reviewer", "  SAM LEE  "),
        ),
        (
            "evidence version",
            "evidence version mismatch",
            changed(GOOD_REVIEW, "evidence_version", 1),
        ),
        (
            "evidence scope",
            "evidence scope mismatch",
            changed(GOOD_REVIEW, "evidence_scope", ("other.txt",)),
        ),
        (
            "evidence operation",
            "evidence scope mismatch",
            changed(GOOD_REVIEW, "evidence_operation", "move"),
        ),
        (
            "evidence source",
            "evidence scope mismatch",
            changed(GOOD_REVIEW, "evidence_source", "other/"),
        ),
        (
            "evidence destination",
            "evidence scope mismatch",
            changed(GOOD_REVIEW, "evidence_destination", "other/"),
        ),
        (
            "evidence publication",
            "evidence scope mismatch",
            changed(GOOD_REVIEW, "evidence_external_publication", True),
        ),
    )
    for name, expected, review in review_cases:
        assert_failure(name, expected, review=review)

    proposal_cases = (
        (
            "network boundary",
            "unsafe boundary",
            changed(PROPOSAL, "network", True),
        ),
        (
            "deletion boundary",
            "unsafe boundary",
            changed(PROPOSAL, "deletes_source", True),
        ),
        (
            "publication boundary",
            "unsafe boundary",
            changed(PROPOSAL, "external_publication", True),
        ),
        (
            "test attestation",
            "tests not recorded as passed",
            changed(PROPOSAL, "tests_passed", False),
        ),
        (
            "recovery attestation",
            "recovery not recorded as tested",
            changed(PROPOSAL, "recovery_tested", False),
        ),
    )
    for name, expected, proposal in proposal_cases:
        assert_failure(name, expected, proposal=proposal)

    # All three records agree in these cases, but independent policy still
    # rejects the jointly changed operation, source, and destination.
    joint_cases = (
        (
            "joint operation change", "operation", "evidence_operation",
            "move", "operation outside policy",
        ),
        (
            "joint source change", "source", "evidence_source",
            "synthetic-ops/other/", "source outside policy",
        ),
        (
            "joint external destination", "destination",
            "evidence_destination", "https://external.example/upload",
            "destination outside policy",
        ),
    )
    for name, field, evidence_field, value, expected in joint_cases:
        proposal, approval, review = jointly_changed(
            field, evidence_field, value
        )
        assert_failure(
            name, expected, proposal=proposal, approval=approval,
            review=review,
        )

    proposal, approval, review = jointly_changed(
        "external_publication", "evidence_external_publication", True
    )
    assert_failure(
        "joint publication change", "unsafe boundary", proposal=proposal,
        approval=approval, review=review,
    )

    # Controlled diagnostics for absent or malformed records and fields.
    assert_failure(
        "missing approval", "approval missing or malformed", approval=None
    )
    assert_failure(
        "missing review", "review missing or malformed", review=None
    )
    assert_failure(
        "missing evidence scope", "review incomplete",
        review={
            key: value for key, value in GOOD_REVIEW.items()
            if key != "evidence_scope"
        },
    )
    assert_failure(
        "null evidence scope", "evidence scope invalid",
        review=changed(GOOD_REVIEW, "evidence_scope", None),
    )
    assert_failure(
        "numeric evidence boolean", "evidence boolean invalid",
        review=changed(
            GOOD_REVIEW, "evidence_external_publication", 0
        ),
    )
    assert_failure(
        "string approval boolean", "approval boolean invalid",
        approval=changed(
            GOOD_APPROVAL, "external_publication", "False"
        ),
    )
    assert_failure(
        "numeric proposal boolean", "proposal boolean invalid",
        proposal=changed(PROPOSAL, "network", 0),
    )
    assert_failure(
        "invalid approval date", "approval date invalid",
        approval=changed(GOOD_APPROVAL, "expires", "2026-09-20"),
    )
    assert_failure(
        "invalid approval scope item", "approval scope invalid",
        approval=changed(GOOD_APPROVAL, "scope", ("alpha.txt", None)),
    )
    assert_failure(
        "unexpected proposal field", "proposal has unexpected fields",
        proposal=dict(PROPOSAL, unapproved=True),
    )


negative_tests()

# Independent positive and failed-fixture assertions.
good = check(
    deepcopy(PROPOSAL), deepcopy(GOOD_APPROVAL), deepcopy(GOOD_REVIEW)
)
bad = check(
    deepcopy(PROPOSAL), deepcopy(BAD_APPROVAL), deepcopy(BAD_REVIEW)
)
assert good == []
assert bad == [
    "approval version mismatch",
    "approval is stale",
    "reviewer is not independent",
    "evidence version mismatch",
]

output_lines = [
    "failed gate: " + "; ".join(bad),
    "repaired gate: " + (
        "APPROVE" if not good else "REJECT: " + "; ".join(good)
    ),
    "bounded scope: archive-manifest-v2, 3 synthetic files, local reversible copy",
]
assert output_lines == [
    "failed gate: approval version mismatch; approval is stale; reviewer is not independent; evidence version mismatch",
    "repaired gate: APPROVE",
    "bounded scope: archive-manifest-v2, 3 synthetic files, local reversible copy",
]
print("\n".join(output_lines))

# Exact expected output:
# failed gate: approval version mismatch; approval is stale; reviewer is not independent; evidence version mismatch
# repaired gate: APPROVE
# bounded scope: archive-manifest-v2, 3 synthetic files, local reversible copy

sections.callout: This is a provider-neutral, offline learning simulation. Its fixture attestations and printed APPROVE result are not actual authorization, production history, or evidence that any review, recovery test, file operation, or target-workstation observation occurred.

sections.title: Compare low, moderate, and high variations
paragraphs: Use the same proposed AI-assisted result to see why the review changes when inputs change. These examples are deliberately bounded and synthetic. They illustrate review proportionality rather than universal thresholds.

LOW variation: the assistant proposes a local copy of three synthetic text files, source files remain unchanged, no network is available, and a human checks that the names and destination are reasonable. A reasonableness check can be sufficient if the described boundary and harms remain true. A missing exact recovery observation should be recorded as UNKNOWN rather than silently treated as tested.

MODERATE variation: the assistant proposes a local copy of 50,000 operational records used by an internal support team. The action remains reversible, but scale, detectability, affected groups, and recovery time increase. Require source comparison, representative and edge-case tests, a named reviewer, a precise allowlist, monitoring, and a tested recovery procedure. If the records contain protected data, the required expertise and controls may increase further; the applicable classification is UNKNOWN until the data and use are established.

HIGH variation: the assistant proposes deleting source records or uploading a generated customer-facing status file. The external or irreversible effect requires current authoritative evidence, independent review, relevant domain expertise, explicit approval, a safe deny-by-default execution boundary, monitoring with a stop signal, and a tested recovery or containment plan. No rollback claim may imply that an external recipient has forgotten or destroyed a disclosed copy.

A change in provider does not by itself change the consequence classification. Switching among Meta, Llama, DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, Phi, NVIDIA, Z.ai, or a hosted system can change the actual tools, data path, retention, access, or automation configuration. Re-run the gate against those concrete facts. Capability, accuracy, and policy behavior are UNKNOWN unless verified for the deployed configuration.

For irreversible actions, prevention and containment are separate from rollback. Before execution, use deny-by-default authorization, an exact human-approved target list, dry-run results, least privilege, and a stop mechanism. After an incident, containment may limit further access or distribution, but it cannot guarantee that an already disclosed copy is destroyed or forgotten.

code.label: Comparison checklist
code.code:
LOW: reasonableness check; local bounded action; detectable and reversible.
MODERATE: source comparison; tests and edge cases; named reviewer; monitoring and tested recovery.
HIGH: current authoritative evidence; independent review; relevant expertise; explicit exact-scope approval; deny-by-default boundary; monitoring and stop signal; tested rollback or containment.

These are practical review-planning labels, not universal legal thresholds or professional advice.

sections.title: Sources and boundaries
paragraphs: This learning resource uses the NIST Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework and its Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile as authoritative risk-management references, and Google's evaluation documentation as a practical evaluation reference. These sources support structured risk identification, evaluation, and management. They do not establish the fictional roles, fixture values, approval dates, universal consequence thresholds, or professional advice in this exercise.

Source dates in this resource identify the supplied verification metadata. A learner should check the linked source and the governing requirements for the actual organization and deployment before relying on them.

The simulation's attestations such as tests_passed and recovery_tested are input records supplied by the fixture. They are not proof that a test or review actually occurred. In a real gate, retain reproducible evidence such as commands, outputs, fixture versions, reviewer identity, comparison results, and execution-boundary observations.

The exercise is provider-neutral and applies the same review logic to Meta, Llama, DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, Phi, NVIDIA, Z.ai, and hosted systems. It makes no unsupported claim about any provider's capabilities, safety, accuracy, privacy, retention, or policy behavior. Verify the actual deployed configuration, including model, prompts, tools, data, logging, permissions, network path, and human process.
